handoff_instructions.purpose: Handoffs document the current state and scope of the project so a new LLM session can pick up exactly where the last one left off. They are the primary continuity mechanism for this project.
what_to_include: A summary of what was done, discussed, decided, or built in this session
What worked and what did not work
Current pipeline state — what scripts exist, what their status is, what the next steps are
A condensed recap of prior sessions so the new LLM has full project context without reading every previous handoff
Open questions or blockers that carry into the next session
what_not_to_include: Exhaustive code listings — reference file paths instead
Decisions that were reversed or abandoned mid-session — only document final state
Speculation about distant future work — stay close to what is actually next
format_rules: This handoff_instructions block must appear at the top of every future handoff
When a user says 'create a handoff for this session,' use this block as the template and fill in the session-specific fields
Prior session summaries should be condensed — one paragraph per session, not a full retelling
Be brief but complete. A new LLM should be able to start working immediately after reading this file

session_context.focus: Statistical knowledge pack extension (Streams 1/2/3) + Solara case library data quality fix

this_session.summary: Two major bodies of work this session: (1) implemented the statistical knowledge pack extension across three parallel streams, and (2) investigated and corrected Solara's wrong scale metrics in the case library.

stream_1_item_prevalence_ls_variance_ite.description: Extended derive_patterns.py with three new sections appended to the knowledge pack JSON
sections_added: item_prevalence — per-item presence counts + conditional breakdowns at portfolio-median ROW_SF and lot_count (thresholds computed dynamically, not hardcoded)
ls_item_variance — CV and OLS regression for LS items with N>=3; CV>0.7 flags high uncertainty, CV>1.0 means analog scaling unreliable
item_scaling — OLS regression of qty vs ROW_SF/lot_count/road_LF for measurable items N>=3; r2>=0.99 flagged as 'derivation rule — near-perfect fit'
key_decisions: Bucket thresholds (ROW_SF median, lot_count median) are computed from portfolio at runtime — not hardcoded. Stored under item_prevalence._thresholds
Phase 2 jobs are NOT excluded from statistical functions — ph2 scope is standalone, ph1 work is not double-counted
Phase 2 special handling remains ONLY in sewer/water per-lot derivation rules (unchanged)

current_knowledge_pack_stats.note: This knowledge pack was generated BEFORE the Solara metrics correction — it must be regenerated

flags_added: ballast_is_separate_pay_item — true if ballast is a separate bid item; false if bundled (e.g. '2/6" paving')
strip_haul_off_required — true if 'INCL HAUL OFF' / 'haul to waste'; false if stockpile
lot_grading_in_scope — true if grading extends onto individual lots ('strip lots', 'rough grade lots')
large_diameter_water_main_present — true if 10" or 12"+ water main shown

changes: Derivation rules now reference item_scaling[...].formula from knowledge pack instead of hardcoded slopes
STRIP ROW: haul-off tier added — strip_haul_off_required=true uses ls_earthwork_rates.row_stripping_haul_off (~$15–25/CY); false uses stockpile rate (~$2.81/CY)
BALLAST: now gated on ballast_is_separate_pay_item=true — fixes Solara $176k false positive
CV guidance added: <0.3 scale confidently; 0.3–0.7 flag ±20%; >0.7 flag ±40%; >1.0 use median with high-uncertainty flag
Lot Grading section added: if lot_grading_in_scope=true include LOT PREP EARTHWORK LS item ±40%
Large-Diameter Water Main section added: if large_diameter_water_main_present=true include separate line item

solara_data_quality_fix.status: complete — file edited, knowledge pack regeneration still pending
solara_data_quality_fix.problem: solara_ph1.json had wrong scale metrics: ROW_SF was 260,188 SF (TAKEOFF column) instead of 304,841 SF (OTHER2/most-recent column), and road_LF excluded Meyer Road frontage which IS included in the ROW polygon
solara_data_quality_fix.root_cause: The Solara ROW polygon includes: internal roads (~238k SF) + Meyer Road frontage dedication (~63.6k SF) + intersections (~3.2k SF) = 304,841 SF total. Meyer Road is an existing public road where the developer must dedicate ROW for widening. It is not an internal road but its area IS in the takeoff polygon.
solara_data_quality_fix.meyer_road_calculation: STA 20+78.68 − STA 11+00 = 978.68 LF of Meyer frontage; internal roads = 2,404.06 LF; new total road_LF = 3,382.74 LF
solara_data_quality_fix.cross_check: 304,841 / 3,382.74 = 90.1 ft — consistent with the C-501 typical section (90 ft ROW + 15 ft sidewalk/drainage each side); also 304,841 × (24/12) / 27 = 22,581 CY stripping matches OTHER2 qty exactly
solara_data_quality_fix.significance: These corrections affect Solara's position in the portfolio (it is now a large-ROW_SF job, not mid-range), the stripping $/CY rate derived from it, and the portfolio medians used for bucket thresholds in item_prevalence. All downstream stats are stale until knowledge pack is regenerated.

what_did_not_work: First attempt used hardcoded ROW_SF_BUCKET_THRESHOLD = 130,000 and LOT_COUNT_BUCKET_THRESHOLD = 35 — rejected by user because it defeats the self-updating purpose. Fixed by computing medians dynamically.
First attempt excluded Phase 2 jobs from item_scaling — rejected because ph2 jobs are standalone. Removed all Phase 2 exclusion from new statistical functions.
Solara's stripping haul-off rate appeared as $9.24/CY (inflated) due to wrong ROW_SF inflating CY denominator — root cause was wrong column (TAKEOFF vs OTHER2) in qty sheet.

prior_sessions_summary.sessions_2026_6_1_through_2026_6_4.5: Built the full Phase 1 pipeline from scratch: Gemini PDF/image extraction (m1/m2/m3), case library in JSON, knowledge pack derivation (derive_patterns.py), and Claude inference system prompt. Established case library with 11 jobs (10 with proposals). Knowledge pack covers unit price distributions, item pairs, derivation rules, LS earthwork rates, paving rates, qty scale correlations, and price trends. Killdeer (25016-2) used as validation holdout throughout.
prior_sessions_summary.session_2026_6_5.1: Tuned m3_infer.py line-item generation — fixed stripping, earthwork, ballast, and sewer/water line items for accuracy. Established that sewer/water scale with lot_count (r=1.0), stripping scales with ROW_SF, earthwork is the hardest LS item to estimate.
prior_sessions_summary.session_2026_6_5.2: Built co-occurrence system in knowledge pack (item_pairs section). Pairs fire when a first item is present to suggest commonly co-occurring items. Identified that ballast being bundled vs. separate is a key source of estimate error.
prior_sessions_summary.session_2026_6_5.3: Test 7 converged on Killdeer — estimate was within ±5% of actual. Discovered Gemini extraction instability (different results on re-run). Identified that Solara was the next job to test. Noted architecture needed rewrite to be more self-updating.
prior_sessions_summary.session_2026_6_5.4: Killdeer fully converged. Started Solara test, discovered $176k ballast false positive (ballast bundled in paving spec, not separate pay item). Architecture rewrite: planned three streams (statistical KP extension, new Gemini flags, system prompt surgery). Streams 1/2/3 all implemented and script ran successfully. Then discovered Solara ROW_SF was wrong (260,188 vs 304,841) — investigation revealed Meyer Road frontage missing from road_LF, wrong qty sheet column used.
prior_sessions_summary.session_2026_6_5.5_this_session: Completed all three architecture streams. Fixed Solara case library: road_LF corrected from 2,404 to 3,382.74 LF (adding Meyer 978.68 LF), ROW_SF corrected from 260,188 to 304,841 (qty sheet OTHER2), road_subgrade_SY from 11,551 to 11,587. Knowledge pack must be regenerated before next validation run.
